```{r setup}
library(gambitR)
```

The puzzle trainer is a small set of tactical positions with verified
solutions, plus a checker that scores an attempt against them.

## Drawing a puzzle

`gm_puzzle()` returns a `gm_puzzle`: the position, the solution as a vector of
moves in standard algebraic notation, a theme and a rating.

```{r}
puzzle <- gm_puzzle(seed = 1)
puzzle
```

```{r}
puzzle$theme
puzzle$rating
puzzle$solution
```

The position is an ordinary `gm_position`, so everything else in the package
applies to it.

```{r}
gm_plot_board(puzzle$position)
gm_status(puzzle$position)
```

## Choosing what to practise

A puzzle can be selected by id, filtered by theme, or drawn at random under a
seed for reproducibility.

```{r}
gm_puzzle(id = "gm-0005")$solution
gm_puzzle(theme = "mateIn2", seed = 1)$solution
identical(gm_puzzle(seed = 42)$id, gm_puzzle(seed = 42)$id)
```

Asking for something that does not exist is an error rather than an empty
draw, and the message lists what is available.

```{r, error = TRUE}
gm_puzzle(theme = "zugzwang")
```

## Checking an attempt

`gm_check_solution()` compares an attempt against the solution as a prefix, so
it reports partial progress rather than a bare pass or fail.

```{r}
fork <- gm_puzzle(id = "gm-0008")
fork$solution
```

```{r}
gm_check_solution(fork, character())
gm_check_solution(fork, fork$solution[1])
gm_check_solution(fork, fork$solution)
```

A wrong first move scores zero, however plausible it looks.

```{r}
gm_check_solution(fork, c("Ne4", "Kg8", "Nxd8"))
```

Check, mate and annotation marks are ignored, so an attempt written `Ra8` is
accepted for a solution written `Ra8#`.

```{r}
back_rank <- gm_puzzle(id = "gm-0001")
gm_check_solution(back_rank, "Ra8")$correct
gm_check_solution(back_rank, "Ra8#!!")$correct
```

## Solving one by hand

Because the solution is just a sequence of moves, it replays like any other
line.

```{r}
position <- fork$position
for (san in fork$solution) {
  position <- gm_move(position, san)
}
gm_plot_board(position)
```

Black's reply in that line is forced: after the knight check the king has
exactly one square, which is why the fork wins the rook.

```{r}
after_check <- gm_move(fork$position, fork$solution[[1]])
gm_legal_moves(after_check)$san
```

## Where the data comes from

The set lives in `inst/extdata/puzzles.rds` and is generated by
`data-raw/puzzles.R`. That script verifies every puzzle against the move
generator before it is written: the position must be legal, each move of the
solution must be legal in turn, every opponent reply must be the only legal
move available, and any line ending in `#` must really end in checkmate. The
Puzzles tab of `gm_run_app()` wraps the same two functions in an interactive
board.
